outcome: The classical uniqueness conjecture remains open, but a genuine (if narrow) necessary condition was proved in the window — Markov's equation is not partition regular (Tao & Yang, Oct 2025) — while the only paper claiming a full resolution (Gore, June 2025) is an unreviewed, uncredentialed math.GM preprint with circular reasoning and no engagement with the literature, and a widely-repeated 'May/June 2026 Heffern 3-adic lifting proof' turned out on verification to be a search-tool hallucination with no corresponding arXiv record.

disputes.summary: Robert A. Gore's 'Patterns Within the Markov Tree' (arXiv:2506.04299, filed under math.GM — arXiv's unendorsed/general-mathematics category, and listing only 'Cheyney, PA' rather than an institutional affiliation) claims in its abstract that analysis of a Pell equation 'leads to the resolution of the Uniqueness Conjecture.' On reading the full text, the argument is circular: it uses Mathematica to observe that solutions to an auxiliary Pell-type equation exist exactly when the parameter equals a Markov number, then treats this observed correspondence as a proof that the parameter must be a Markov number, without independently establishing uniqueness of the corresponding triple. It cites no foundational literature (Frobenius, Aigner, Cohn, Christoffel-word / cluster-algebra work) beyond a single Quanta Magazine article, and has not been digested, endorsed, or cited by any specialist. It has not been treated as a resolution by the community and does not meet the bar for `resolved` or even `claimed` credibility, but is recorded here as a claim that surfaced in the window.

summary: The classical uniqueness (Frobenius/unicity) conjecture for Markov numbers is still open as of this research. Several genuine but non-resolving pieces of work appeared in the window (26 Jan 2024 – present): (1) David Fisac's 'Markov's Conjecture on integral necklaces' (arXiv:2501.15550, submitted 26 Jan 2025, revised Feb and Aug 2025) reformulates the geometric simple-length-spectrum version of the conjecture into purely combinatorial terms — a reformulation, not a proof, and its own abstract makes no resolution claim; this is a related restatement rather than a case settled, so on its own it would not move status. (2) Daniel Martin's 'A new proof of Chen's theorem for Markoff graphs' (arXiv:2502.15960, Feb 2025) is not about the uniqueness conjecture at all — it gives an alternate proof that connected components of the Markoff mod-p graph have size divisible by p (Chen's 2021 result), which bears on graph connectivity/Baragar's conjecture, a different problem; the triage's uncertainty about its scope is resolved here as 'not this problem.' (3) Tianyi Tao and Bohan Yang, 'Markov's equation is not partition regular' (arXiv:2510.10151, submitted 11 Oct 2025), prove that no finite coloring of the positive integers has every color class containing a solution of the Markov equation, and state explicitly that this 'confirms a necessary condition for the Uniqueness Conjecture' — this is genuine incremental progress narrowing what any full proof must be compatible with, though it does not settle any case of the conjecture itself (no specific Markov number's uniqueness is newly established), so it is coded `progress` rather than `partial`. (4) Robert A. Gore's 'Patterns Within the Markov Tree' (arXiv:2506.04299, math.GM, June/Aug 2025) explicitly claims in its abstract to resolve the Uniqueness Conjecture, but on reading the full text the argument is circular (observing via Mathematica that an auxiliary equation's solutions correspond to Markov numbers, then treating that correspondence as the proof), engages with essentially no specialist literature, and has had no expert digestion or endorsement — it does not meet the bar for `resolved`, and given how far short it falls of even a serious unreviewed claim, it is noted as a dispute/curiosity rather than driving the status to `claimed`. No AI system is credited with any mathematics in any of these four items: Gore explicitly credits Mathematica (a computer algebra system, not an AI system under §6.2) for exploratory pattern-finding, and Tao & Yang's paper shows no sign of AI involvement in its methodology section. Separately, an initial web search returned a confident-sounding claim that 'Elleard Heffern' published a proof of the unicity conjecture via 3-adic lifting in May/June 2026; this was checked directly against the arXiv API (search for author Heffern) and returned zero results, and the named 'Elleard Heffern' is verifiably a biology PhD student (bird-flock phase transitions, Royal Society B) with no known number-theory work — this claim is a hallucination produced by the search tool's synthesis and is excluded from the record entirely per instructions to verify primary sources. No DeepMind/OpenAI/Anthropic system (AlphaEvolve, AlphaProof, etc.) has been reported working on this specific conjecture; those systems' 2025-2026 results (Kakeya, Erdős problems) are on unrelated problems. Because the only event that is both real and squarely on-topic (Tao & Yang) is a necessary-condition result narrowing the space rather than settling a case, status is coded `progress` with `ai_role` `none`.
competing_reading: One could argue Fisac's reformulation should also be logged as an `event` alongside Tao & Yang's, since a successful reformulation can be instrumental to eventual resolution; it is described in `disputes`/summary instead of as a second `event` per the instruction to describe multiple events in `summary` rather than invent extra records. One could also argue the Gore paper, despite its flaws, should be coded `claimed` rather than left out of `status` — the record instead treats it as a dispute over credibility because it shows no sign of having been taken seriously by anyone (no citations, no digestion, unendorsed category), which is different from a serious claimed proof awaiting review.
what_would_settle_it: An expert digestion (blog post, referee report, or citation by a specialist) either endorsing or debunking the Gore paper's argument would resolve whether it belongs in the record at all; a subsequent paper building on Tao & Yang's partition-regularity result to settle an actual case of uniqueness (e.g., for a new infinite family of Markov numbers) would move status to `partial`.
